originality.rationale: The broad fact that damping ratios measure asymptotic rates rather than case-specific transient durations is established in prior matrix-population literature. The new claim is narrower and source-specific: for the reducible perfect-transmission Wolbachia CTMC it derives the missing mixed-class entry/eigenvector coefficient in closed form, proves that this coefficient controls the class-mass ratio, and shows by an exact same-architecture CTMC that the Table 5 gap-only class-mass time is not determined by the gap. Searches found the motivating source and broad damping-ratio cautions, but no prior statement of this source-specific formula or correction.
residual_risks: Caswell's book was not inspected in full; it may contain a generic coefficient-sensitive spectral formula. That would reinforce the mathematics but would not by itself establish that this Wolbachia Table 5 application included the required mixed-start amplitude.
No source-specific correction or erratum was located in the searches performed.
